tasks.short: Prepare logs of the work performed.

steps.what: Prepare the facts of work performed.
Draft the documentation from that field note.

loop.input: The fault, the parts and the times she noted in s1, in her own words.
loop.output: Log lines that quote only those facts and say what work was performed.
loop.check: Each line quotes a fault, a part or a time she noted, and says what work was performed. A line that adds a cause, a part, a time or a site she did not note fails. A suggested fault code that is not on the stored list fails.
loop.stop: One pass. A failing line is dropped and not repaired. If every line fails, the draft stays blank and she writes the log.
loop.why_not_simpler: A field copy cannot say what work was performed.

steps.what: Check the documentation quotes only that note.
Confirm these logs and these reports.
File these logs in the maintenance system.

tasks.design: She notes the fault, the parts and the times on site. A draft in {DOCS} writes log lines that quote only those facts, and she confirms the logs and the reports. A separate write files only that confirmed log in the maintenance system ({OTHER}).
tasks.previous_blocker: The fault, the parts and the times sat in a notebook or a voice note, and the log was typed up later.
tasks.enabler_now: A note with those facts lets a draft quote them, and the file waits for the log she confirms.
tasks.still_hard: She still notes the job on site. A fault code that is not on the list stays blank. She still confirms the log.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which fault the pick list flattens, and which part she actually fitted.

ambition.what: She confirms the log before she leaves the plant, on jobs where the fault and the parts are already noted.

tasks.altitude: Confirming the log stays hers. Only the draft and the file move.

reach.task: Keep the fault-code list for closed jobs
reach.learn: Which code she refused because it did not fit

reach.task: Read the log she filed for the shift
reach.learn: Which job she closed before she left

evidence.claim: Ultimo records preventive plans and repair history on mobile work orders.
MaintainX transcribes a voice memo into the work order and asks the technician to confirm an unusual reading.
Work orders with time stamps or location can observe technicians, and works-council consent comes first.

Drafting a log from facts she noted is not the repair. This range uses neither the food-plant downtime figure nor the fibre-network hours. The file stores the times she confirmed and does not store her location.

assumptions: Before the draft she notes job, asset, fault, parts, start time and stop time in her own words. The planner keeps the fault-code list. A code that is not on the list is left blank, and she types any line the draft dropped.

The file writes only the log she confirmed. It does not send a message, it does not post to the ledger, and it does not store her location. Start and stop are the times she noted, not a clock that follows her. No unusual-reading alert is sent.
The planner's list upkeep is other-role time below. Her one incremental hour is a part she remembers after she has confirmed the log.
unknowns: Whether the works council treats start and stop times on a work log as monitoring, even with no location.
research_questions: Which faults on the current list still have no code the technicians will use?

already_counted.description: Reading each log line against the field note and striking a cause, a part or a time she did not note.

incremental.description: Rewriting a log when she remembers a part after she has confirmed it.
Planner keeps the fault-code list and adds a code when none fits.

approvals.approved_version: The log she confirmed in s4 for the fault, parts and times she noted in s1. A change to those facts voids this approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A shift where she has already noted the fault, the parts and the times for each job. Low is a call-out night with no note, so she writes the log by hand. High is that shift, and the note and the confirm do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Name the plant equipment that has failed.
Fetch repair history for that plant equipment.
Check the history is that plant equipment.
Identify malfunctions in the plant controls.
Correct those malfunctions on the equipment.

tasks.design: She names the equipment that has failed. A fetch from the maintenance system ({OTHER}) writes the repair history for that asset only, and she checks it is the same equipment. She identifies the malfunction and corrects it on the plant herself.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repair history sat in closed logs she could not open while she stood at the equipment.
tasks.enabler_now: A closed log tied to the asset can be fetched once she names the equipment.
tasks.still_hard: Finding the fault and correcting it stay on the plant. A new failure with no history leaves the card blank.
tasks.human_edge: She hears the plant and knows which reading is the fault rather than the weather.
tasks.altitude: The diagnosis and the repair stay hers. Only the history card moves.

reach.task: Keep each closed log tied to the asset
reach.learn: Which equipment she is standing at

reach.task: Isolate the circuit she names before she works on it
reach.learn: Which equipment she is about to open

evidence.claim: Ultimo records preventive plans and repair history on mobile work orders.
A history card is not the diagnosis and not the repair. This range uses no downtime figure.

assumptions: The fetch uses only the asset she named in s1. The card is blank when that asset has no closed log. The fault-code list is kept on the log task and is not counted again here.
She identifies and corrects the fault herself. The card does not suggest a repair, it does not open a permit, and it does not send an alert.
The one incremental hour is opening a second asset when the first card was the wrong equipment.
unknowns: Whether closed logs on this plant are already stored against the asset, or only against the shift date.
research_questions: Which assets that failed this year still have no closed log tied to them?

already_counted.description: Reading the history card and rejecting it when the asset is not the equipment she named.

incremental.description: Opening the history for a second asset when the first card was the wrong equipment.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A fault on equipment that already has a closed log. Low is a first failure with no history, so the card is blank. High is that known asset, and identifying and correcting the fault do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record operating data from the wells.

steps.what: Collect readings across these well fields.
Fetch stored power readings for these fields.
Fill the operating sheet for these plants.
Check each operating line against those fields.
Record the checked readings for these plants.

tasks.design: She collects the readings she takes by hand and names the wells. A fetch from the plant historian ({OTHER}) returns only tags marked as streaming, and the {SPREADSHEET} fills the operating sheet from those tags plus her hand readings. She checks every line, and a separate write records only the checked readings in the plant historian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Well readings were a paper round that she copied onto a sheet the next morning.
tasks.enabler_now: Tags the operator has marked as streaming can be copied, and her hand readings still fill the gaps.
tasks.still_hard: She still walks the wells that have no feed. She still judges a reading that looks wrong. No alert is sent.
tasks.human_edge: She sees a well the tag has not caught, and she knows which swing is the field rather than a bad sensor.
tasks.altitude: The round stays hers. The operating sheet and the plant-log write move, and the write waits for her check.

reach.task: Mark which plant tags already stream
reach.learn: Which wells she still walks by hand

reach.task: Name the wells on today's round

evidence.claim: Copying a stored plant tag onto a sheet is not the well-field round. No source in this digest reads a geothermal well, and this range uses no vendor time figure.

assumptions: Before the fetch she names the well and writes the reading she took by hand. The historian returns a value only for a tag the control-room operator has marked as streaming. A tag with no feed stays blank, and she keeps the hand reading.

The operating sheet is a draft. The plant-log write stores only the readings she checked, for the wells she named. It does not send an out-of-range alert and it does not store her route or her location.
The operator's tag-map upkeep is other-role time below. Her one incremental hour is a well the operator marks as streaming only after the round.
unknowns: Whether this plant historian can return a value for a tag without her opening the control screen.
research_questions: Which wells on the current round have no tag marked as streaming?

already_counted.description: Reading each operating line against the well she walked and the hand reading she wrote.

incremental.description: Adding a well the operator marks as streaming only after she has finished the round.
Control-room operator marks which plant tags already stream.

approvals.approved_version: The readings she accepted in s4 for the wells she named in s1. A change to those readings voids this approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A round where most wells already have a streaming tag and she has walked the rest. Low is a field with almost no feed, so she writes every reading. High is that round, and the walk and the check do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide if auxiliary heat is needed.

steps.what: Name the properties, the weather and the systems.
Fill load lines for those auxiliary systems.
Check the lines name only those properties.
Determine whether auxiliary systems are needed.
Tell the sites which properties need cover.

tasks.design: She names the properties, the weather and the auxiliary capacity. The {SPREADSHEET} fills a load line from only those figures, and she checks it adds no property. She determines whether auxiliary systems are needed and tells the sites herself.
tasks.previous_blocker: The weather call sat in her head, and the auxiliary capacity sat in a site folder.
tasks.enabler_now: Once she writes the load and the capacity, a sheet can place them on one line.
tasks.still_hard: She still decides, and she still tells the sites. A property with no capacity stays blank. The sheet does not start a system.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which building can coast and which one cannot lose heat tonight.
tasks.altitude: The weather call stays hers. Only the load sheet moves, and it does not start a system.

reach.task: Name the auxiliary capacity of the property
reach.learn: Which property she has decided to cover

reach.task: Hold the design load for each property
reach.learn: Which weather she is planning for

evidence.claim: A load line from figures she typed is not the decision to start an auxiliary system. No source in this digest makes that weather call, and the sheet does not start anything.

assumptions: Before the sheet she writes property, expected weather, design load and auxiliary capacity. A missing capacity leaves that property blank. The sheet uses only figures she wrote.
The sheet is a draft in her hand. It does not send a message, it does not page a site, and it does not start an auxiliary system. She tells the sites herself.
The one incremental hour is a property whose capacity arrives after she has checked the sheet.
unknowns: Whether she is allowed to start the auxiliary plant, or only the site contact is.
research_questions: Which properties on the heat-pump list have no auxiliary capacity written down?

already_counted.description: Reading each load line and striking a property or a figure she did not write.

incremental.description: Adding a property whose capacity arrives after she has checked the sheet.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A cold week where she has already written the load and the auxiliary capacity for each property. Low is a warning that arrives with no capacities on file. High is that week, and the decision and the calls to the sites do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still the plant round, the repair and the weather call. Only the log draft, the log file, the history card, the operating sheet, the plant-log write and the load sheet move.
reach: The planner keeps the fault-code list and leaves a code blank when none fits the fault she noted.
The control-room operator marks which plant tags already stream, and a tag with no mark stays blank.
The site contact names the auxiliary capacity of each property before the load sheet is filled.
The well-field lead names the wells on the round she is about to walk.
skills_to_grow: Reject a log line that adds a fault, a part or a time she did not note.
Reject a history card for equipment she did not name, and still find the fault herself.
Reject an operating line for a well she did not walk and that no stored tag returned.
Refuse a load sheet that would start an auxiliary system, and make that call herself.
role.ambitious_version: When she has noted the fault and the parts, she confirms the log before she leaves the plant, and the repair, the well round and the weather call stay hers.
